title: Durban Lamb and Potato Bunny Chow
summary: A warming Durban-style lamb and potato curry piled into a hollowed loaf of bread, finished with a fresh carrot sambal for crunch and zing.
equipment: mortar and pestle or rolling pin and bag

ingredients.item: boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 2 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp cumin seeds and 10 black peppercorns in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, then cool and crush coarsely.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pan and cook 1 chopped onion until soft and golden, 8-10 min.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Stir in 4 chopped garlic cloves and 1½ tbsp chopped ginger and cook for 1 min.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Raise the heat, add 700 g cubed lamb shoulder and brown on all sides, 8-10 min.

steps.title: Spice
steps.text: Stir in the crushed spices with ¾ tsp turmeric, a 3 cm cinnamon stick, 1 tsp chilli powder and 1¼ tsp salt and cook for 1 min.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add 400 g potatoes, 240 g yoghurt, 120 ml milk and 120 ml coconut milk, cover and simmer gently until the lamb and potatoes are tender, 35-45 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, spring onions and most of the coriander leaves.

steps.title: Sambal
steps.text: Toss the grated carrots with the chopped green chilli, lemon juice and salt.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Cut the loaf into 4 blocks, hollow each one, fill with curry, top with the bread lid and serve alongside the sambal.

tips: Brown the lamb in batches if the pan feels crowded so it colours rather than stews.
Taste the sauce before filling the loaf, as the yoghurt mellows the spice as it cooks.
Keep the scooped-out bread to use as a lid, or tear it up for dunking.
storage: Keep any leftover curry covered in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat gently until piping hot (74°C) before filling fresh bread. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
